info.name: CityCare API
info.description:
CityCare — a municipal complaint and service platform.

**How to use this collection**

1. Import `citycare.postman_environment.json` too, and select **CityCare — local** top right.
2. Run folder **01 — Setup** top to bottom. The three logins fill `adminToken`, `officerToken` and `citizenToken` automatically — each login reads the role out of its own response and stores the token where that role's requests expect it.
3. Then work down the folders in order, 02 to 10. Ids are captured as you go (`complaintId`, `categoryId`, `paymentId` …) and path parameters read them, so nothing needs to be copied by hand.

Every request asserts its own status code, so the Tests tab is green or red at a glance and the Collection Runner can run a whole folder.

⚠ marks a request that deletes something or invalidates your token. Run those last, then re-run folder 01.

Seeded logins: `admin@citycare.com` / `Admin@12345`, `officer1@citycare.com` / `Officer@12345`, `citizen1@citycare.com` / `Citizen@12345`.

Full walkthrough: `docs/postman-guide.md` in the repository.

item.description: Signup is Redis-first: nothing reaches PostgreSQL until the OTP is verified. Without SMTP the OTP is printed in the dev server log — paste it into the `otp` variable. The last four requests are marked ⚠ because they invalidate {{citizenToken}}; run them when you are done with the rest and then re-run folder 01.

A pre-request script puts a fresh address in {{signupEmail}}, so this never hits 409 EMAIL_EXISTS.

The password policy is 10+ characters with an upper case letter, a lower case letter, a digit and a symbol, and it must not contain your name or the local part of your email — put "Rahim" in the password and this is a 400.

Read the OTP from the inbox, or from the dev server log, and put it in the `otp` variable.

item.name: 05 — Complaint
item.description: The core of the system. Run the sub-folders in order and one complaint travels from SUBMITTED to CLOSED. Who may make which move is fixed by a state machine — see docs/postman-guide.md §5.

item.description: The citizen reports, then everyone reads it through the view their role allows.

{
  "title": "Road e boro gorto",
  "description": "Mirpur 10 golchottor er pashe 3 foot gorto, rickshaw ulte jacche",
  "categoryId": "{{categoryId}}",

request.description:
Saves {{complaintId}} and {{trackingId}}.

**Idempotency.** Send it a second time without changing anything: the answer is byte-identical, carries the header `Idempotent-Replay: true`, and no second complaint is filed. Edit the body but keep the same {{idempotencyKey}} and it is 422 IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH.

The stored answer lives for 24 hours, so **to file a genuinely new complaint later, change `idempotencyKey` in the environment** — otherwise you keep getting the first one back.

**409 DUPLICATE_COMPLAINT** is the other guard: the same citizen already has an *open* complaint in this category and ward from the last 24 hours. Finish the lifecycle sub-folder (a closed complaint no longer blocks), pick another wardId, or log in as citizen2.

exec: console.log("REPLAY — this is the stored answer to an earlier send of idempotencyKey \"" +
pm.environment.get("idempotencyKey") + "\". Change that variable to file a new complaint.");

item.name: Lifecycle — run these in order
item.description: SUBMITTED → UNDER_REVIEW (admin) → ASSIGNED (admin) → IN_PROGRESS (officer) → RESOLVED (officer, with proof) → CLOSED (citizen feedback). Anything else is 409 INVALID_TRANSITION, and a role that is not allowed the move is 403.

request.description: 409 once it has moved past SUBMITTED.

item.name: 02. Move the complaint — SUBMITTED to UNDER_REVIEW (ADMIN)

request.description:
Then re-send this same request three more times, editing two things each time:

1. status IN_PROGRESS, Authorization {{officerToken}} — only after the assign step below
2. status RESOLVED, {{officerToken}} — 409 until a RESOLUTION_PROOF attachment exists
3. status CLOSED, {{adminToken}} — or let the citizen's feedback close it

Send it with {{officerToken}} right now and it is 403: SUBMITTED to UNDER_REVIEW is an admin move.

`"auto": true` picks the least-loaded active officer in the category's own department, so this request works on its own.

To assign by hand instead, send `{"officerId": "{{officerId}}", "auto": false, "reason": "…"}` — run **09 — Admin → Users → 01. List users** first to fill {{officerId}}. An officer from another department is a 409: a Roads complaint cannot land on the Waste desk.

Assigning from UNDER_REVIEW or REOPENED also moves the status to ASSIGNED.
Every hop, who made it, when, and the note.
Within 7 days, at most twice — both limits are runtime settings a super admin can change.
409 once it has moved on — cancelling is a citizen's move out of SUBMITTED only.
⚠ It vanishes from every query. A super admin can bring it back with 09 — Admin → Super admin only → Restore.

item.description: Evidence belongs to the owner, resolution proof to the assigned officer, and internal notes never reach a citizen.

request.description: form-data, field `file`, plus `kind`. EVIDENCE is the owner's; RESOLUTION_PROOF must come from the assigned officer, so switch to {{officerToken}} for that one. Five per complaint. 503 means Cloudinary is not configured.
HTML is stripped before storage. Set "isInternal": true with {{officerToken}} to leave a staff-only note.
Fetch it with {{citizenToken}} and the internal note is not in the response; fetch it with {{officerToken}} and it is.
